ev.q: Overall, 36.7% of U.S. adults or 78.1 million persons aged ≥21 years were on or eligible for cholesterol treatment.
There were significant differences in the percentage of men (40.8%) and women (32.9%; p≤0.001) on or eligible for treatment
the proportion taking cholesterol-lowering medication between men and women (52.9% versus 58.6%; p = 0.010)
among the estimated 78 million U.S. adults aged ≥21 years eligible for treatment, 55.5% were taking cholesterol-lowering medication
significant differences in the proportion taking cholesterol-lowering medication between men and women
Prevalence of cholesterol-lowering medication use among adults eligible for treatment varied within sex and racial/ethnic subgroups
NHANES is an ongoing national survey using a complex, multistage, probability sampling design

methods_quotes.q: Pearson's chi-square test was used to determine significant differences (p<0.05) across sex and racial/ethnic groups.
Analyses were performed using fasting sample weights and adjusted variance estimates to account for complex sampling.
Population counts were estimated using population totals provided from NHANES and averaging the population during the time coinciding with the four NHANES cycles.
Estimates statistically unstable with relative standard error ≥30%
